🇲🇽🛢️ <u>US Says It Sold Mexico 597,000 Barrels of Crude. Pemex Says It Bought None</u>

US Census records show 597,027 barrels of crude, worth $69.67 million, exported to Mexico in June 2026 through New Orleans. It is the first such entry since 2018. Pemex says it has imported no crude this year and has no record of a valid permit, El Financiero reports. According to the same report, SENER, the Energy Ministry, has issued no crude import permits to Pemex or to any private firm. So who is the buyer, and where did the oil go?

🇲🇽✊ <u>IMSS Workers Reject 2.9% Raise, March in 12 States</u>

Active and retired workers at IMSS, Mexico's social security institute, protested across 12 states and Mexico City on October 8 against the 2.9% raise their union leadership accepted. They are demanding 10%. Talks at Gobernación, the interior ministry, ran more than seven hours and ended with no deal. Workers say the approved raise works out to 120–160 extra pesos per pay period. They also denounced shortages of medicine and supplies. They announced rolling work stoppages, with emergency rooms, inpatient wards and operating rooms kept running.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Operación Enjambre: 1,208 Years in Prison for 27 People in Edomex</u>

State of Mexico prosecutors have won convictions totaling 1,208 years and 10 months against 27 people, including former mayors, police chiefs and municipal officials, for homicide, kidnapping, extortion and forced disappearance. The operation began in November 2024 after the remains of 10 people were found in wells in Nicolás Romero. Former Amanalco mayor María Elena Martínez Robles got 70 years for killing members of her own administration.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>GM Corn Case Against Monsanto Heads to Mexico's Supreme Court</u>

A federal appeals court voted unanimously to ask the Supreme Court (SCJN) to take over the 13-year-old class action against GM corn. The suit was filed in 2013 by 53 people and more than 20 organizations against the agriculture and environment ministries and Monsanto (now Bayer), Dow AgroSciences, Syngenta and PHI-México. The judges cited the case's national relevance. The precautionary measure the Court upheld in 2021 is still in force: no commercial permits to release transgenic corn while the case is decided.

🇲🇽💧 <u>Federal Government Steps In on Guadalajara's Water Crisis</u>

Sheinbaum says an agreement with Jalisco to tackle the contaminated-water crisis in the Guadalajara metro area is in its final phase, with Conagua working on the fix. Under the deal, the federal government will build and pay for the pending works that bring the El Zapotillo system to 100% capacity. Governor Pablo Lemus says it means no new public debt, no rate hikes at SIAPA, the local water utility, and no privatization of the service.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Heavy Truck Exports Up 144.6% in September</u>

Mexico shipped 12,707 buses, trucks and tractor-trailers abroad in September, up from 5,196 a year earlier, according to ANPACT, the industry association. That is the biggest jump of 2026. Production rose 121%, to 15,181 units. January–September exports reached 98,394 units, up 12%. Tariffs or not, North America's freight still rides on Mexican-built trucks.

🇲🇽🌎 "Within the framework of our Constitution... territorial integrity, respect for sovereignty, mutual trust and coordination without subordination." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 Sheinbaum said she gave these numbers to business leaders and US Ambassador Ronald Johnson at Palacio Nacional on Thursday. Irregular border crossings are down 98%, and fentanyl seizures in the US are down 75% because of operations on the Mexican side. There are "mirror operations" since Trump sent the US Army to the border, and some 94 major drug bosses have been sent to the US. The cooperation runs under Mexico's Constitution and the National Security Law. What Mexico wants now is for the US to lower its tariffs on cars and steel.

🔥🇲🇽 "How is he going to talk about democracy? The one who committed electoral fraud?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 Asked about former presidents Zedillo, Calderón, Salinas and Fox speaking out against the 4T, Sheinbaum laid out the record. Fox reached power in 2000 with Zedillo's help and promised democracy. Four years later came the desafuero, an invented crime used to try to keep López Obrador, then Mexico City's head of government, off the 2006 ballot, until mass protests forced Fox to back down. Then came the 2006 electoral fraud. "How is Calderón going to talk about democracy if he came to power with electoral fraud? How is Salinas?" She said it matters to remember, because an 18-year-old today was born under Calderón.

🇲🇽⚖️ "It is not rhetoric, it is principles... A people without memory has no compass." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 A Revista Zócalo reporter said critics call her talk of sovereignty and independence a rhetorical device against Trump's threats. Sheinbaum answered that Mexico faced threats from foreign powers in the 19th and 20th centuries, that the neoliberal period opened the door to economic policy being set from abroad, and that the Calderón years opened it to US agencies operating freely on Mexican territory. The president has to keep that principle present "so that the people of Mexico have the memory of what our independence and our sovereignty have cost us." She added that 42 million people now receive a well-being program directly.
banner: "IT IS NOT RHETORIC, IT IS PRINCIPLES"
